tasks.title: A stalled request body is never timed out once the head is counted in flight
tasks.discovered-by: lead from the credit-terminated server reviewer, re-derived in the current tree by the main agent
tasks.evidence-before: channelRead resets the 120-second idle deadline on every read and increments inFlightRequests when a valid head arrives. resetIdleDeadline's scheduled task closes only when inFlightRequests == 0 and is not re-armed after it fires. A client that sends headers plus a partial body therefore leaves inFlightRequests == 1 forever: the timer fires, declines to close, and nothing else closes the connection. The up-to-1 MiB body buffer and the connection are held indefinitely. The comment above resetIdleDeadline claims a stalled slowloris request is closed, which this path cannot do. Loopback-only binding limits the blast radius, but this is local denial of service and contradicts the stated S1 control.
tasks.fix-summary: No fix applied. Add a body-completion deadline (or re-arm while a body is incomplete), distinct from the no-in-flight idle close, and keep the never-close-mid-generation rule.
tasks.evidence-after: Verified by code path only; no live stalled-client probe was run.

tasks.title: CLI Ctrl-C cancels the outer task, so an in-flight generation keeps running
tasks.discovered-by: lead from the credit-terminated library reviewer, re-derived in the current tree by the main agent
tasks.evidence-before: The SIGINT handler cancels only the task that drives run(args:). Session.respond wraps generation in an unstructured Task and awaits work.value; cancellation does not propagate into an unstructured task, and awaiting Task.value in a cancelled task does not throw. The CLI never calls Session.cancel(), which is the path the server uses. A long generation therefore ignores SIGINT until it finishes on its own.
tasks.fix-summary: No fix applied. Either call session.cancel() from the SIGINT handler or replace runOneShot with a cancellation-forwarding structure and keep the .cancelled mapping.
tasks.evidence-after: Static trace only; a CLI SIGINT probe against the installed 4B was not executed.

tasks.title: PLE prefill gather is bounded by the scratch chunk size, not by the PLEBlock rows it writes
tasks.discovered-by: lead from the credit-terminated inference reviewer, re-derived in the current tree by the main agent
tasks.evidence-before: PLEBlock allocates embedding = embedDim * maxRows with maxRows = runtimeConfiguration.prefillChunkTokens. executePrefillChunk checks tokens.count against scratch.layout.chunkTokens, which is built from the caller's PrefillRuntimeConfig; production(chunkTokens:) accepts any value in allowedPrefillChunkTokens independently of the runner's own configuration. gatherPLERowsPrefill then writes tokens.count rows of headCount*rowBytes into that buffer. A caller passing a chunk larger than the runner's configured prefillChunkTokens passes the scratch guard and writes past the PLE embedding allocation in host-visible shared Metal memory.
tasks.fix-summary: No fix applied. Bound the gather by PLEBlock.maxRows (or size PLEBlock from the effective chunk) and refuse a config whose chunkTokens exceeds the runner's.
tasks.evidence-after: Static analysis only. Shipped front ends appear to pass the engine's own prefillChunkTokens, so reachability requires a caller that constructs a mismatched PrefillRuntimeConfig; RealForwardRunner is public in the engine target but is not part of the TinyTitanLib facade.
